subject: NotObserved is unreachable in practice on unelevated scans
decision: Ship P21-N3 as built. FR-74 is correct and stays; do NOT relax is_complete() to a percentage threshold to make NotObserved attainable. Record that the three-state model collapses to Loaded/Unknown on any scan where coverage is incomplete.
rationale: Measured on a real desktop unelevated: 159 of 332 processes readable, 6 findings Loaded, 0 NotObserved, 982 Unknown. Because FR-74 forces every non-match to Unknown when coverage is incomplete, NotObserved can only occur when readable == total. Even elevated, Windows protected processes (PPL, antimalware) typically cannot be opened, so full coverage may be unattainable in practice. The consequence is that the feature can promote loaded findings but can never report a finding as dormant, so only half the roadmap's noise-reduction premise is realised. Relaxing the completeness test would restore the other half at the cost of reintroducing exactly the false-negative FR-74 exists to prevent, on a signal that is a seconds-long sample of a months-long runtime.
cost_if_wrong: The noise-reduction benefit stays limited to promotion only (6 of 988 findings on the measured host). Recoverable at any time: is_complete() is one function, and a future change could introduce a coverage threshold or per-directory completeness tracking without touching the enum, the matching rules, or the reports.

summary: Runtime reachability shipped across six tasks (7d8cd18..416705f). Three-state Reachability enum with a partial-coverage Unknown floor; local collection via direct kernel32/advapi32 Toolhelp32 FFI (no new dependency, TH32CS_SNAPMODULE32 included so WOW64 processes are seen); remote collection over WinRM with a fixed non-interpolated script block (SEC-8); a strictly >=1.0 risk multiplier so no finding can ever be demoted; reachability in text/CSV/JSON/HTML; --no-reachability and coverage disclosure. Every load-bearing rule mutation-verified: forcing NotObserved on partial coverage, basename matching instead of exact path, a 0.8 factor for Unknown, and delta_known-dependent VEX state all fail their guards. 377 workspace tests pass, clippy -D warnings clean. Verified on real data: 159/332 processes readable unelevated, multiplier exact (23.0->28.7, 22.7->28.4, 21.3->26.6, 21.8->27.2, 3.2->4.0). CONCERN: only 6 of 988 findings reached Loaded and 0 reached NotObserved, because incomplete coverage forces every non-match to Unknown. The three-state model therefore collapses to two states on any unelevated scan, so the roadmap's noise-reduction premise is only half realised — we can promote running code but can never report a finding as dormant. Recorded as a ruling; needs a human call on whether that is acceptable or whether coverage handling should change.

Cross-asset remediation aggregation shipped in three tasks (725450d..9bb7c42). `toonable fleet report` groups stored findings across every scanned host and ranks upgrades by total risk removed, in text or JSON. Risk is derived at report time from the current CVE database and never persisted (FR-84), so the rollup can never disagree with reassess about the same finding. Criticality resolves per host from fleet tags; reachability is structurally Unknown since FR-82 forbids persisting it. Unscoreable CVEs are excluded AND counted (FR-87) rather than scored as zero. Three mutations verified: keying on (name, version) splits one Chrome action into three; sorting by cve_count inverts breadth against depth; narrowing the status filter to Resolved alone readmits NoLongerApplicable rows. 387 workspace tests pass, clippy clean. Verified end to end on the real scan_history.db. CONCERN — display-name aliasing double-counts risk. The live report shows "Microsoft Edge" and "Microsoft Edge Update" as separate rows, each 221 CVEs and 2509.4 risk removed; likewise PostgreSQL/PostgreSQL 16, Microsoft Edge Installer/Stable, and Visual Studio Code/Microsoft Visual Studio Code (User). These are one product under several registry display names, so a reader sees ~5018 of available risk reduction where only ~2509 exists. This is inherent to grouping by display name, which is all scan_findings stores; the per-asset Top Solutions view has the same flaw. Fixing it properly requires persisting the matched CPE product identity alongside each finding — a schema change that cuts against FR-84's premise of storing no derived data. Needs a human call.

subject: MSRC ingest is opt-in and never redistributed (P21-N5)
decision: Build MSRC CVRF ingestion in cve-db-builder behind an explicit --enable-msrc flag, off by default, printing the Microsoft APIs Terms of Use notice on first use. Toonable SHALL NEVER ship or distribute a database containing MSRC-derived data; every user syncs their own, exactly as with NVD and FKIE-CAD. Where MSRC has a verdict for a (CVE, product) pair it overrides the NVD/CPE match; absence of an MSRC row falls back to NVD rather than suppressing the finding.
rationale: Microsoft APIs Terms of Use section 3(b)(14) flatly prohibits redistributing data obtained via the API, and 3(b)(4) permits building a database only "as necessary to enable an intended usage scenario for your Application". A locally-synced offline scanner cache is squarely an intended usage scenario, and the sync-only architecture satisfies 3(b)(14) by construction. Applicability is genuinely ambiguous: section 1(d) enumerates the governed APIs and MSRC CVRF is not among them, while section 1(b)'s broad definition arguably sweeps it in, and no MSRC-specific accompanying terms could be located. The general Microsoft website ToU is more restrictive still, saying personal and non-commercial use. Making acceptance an affirmative act via an opt-in flag rather than a side effect of running a sync is the defensible position if the tool is ever sold. Technically verified as sound: MSRC gives an exact FixedBuild and KB per CVE, and every MSRC CPE product string resolves in the existing NVD dictionary after lowercasing, so ProductID to CPE to matcher identity is a real bridge.
cost_if_wrong: If the terms are later read as prohibiting even local caching for commercial users, the feature must be disabled — but because it is opt-in and ships no data, no distributed artifact would need recall and no user would be in breach without having affirmatively enabled it. If MSRC coverage proves thinner than NVD for some product, the fallback rule means findings are never lost, only left at NVD precision.

title: MSRC storage tables and incremental upserts (DC-8, FR-90)

title: CVRF document parsing (FR-90, FR-96)
description: Create cve-db-builder/src/msrc/parse.rs plus a trimmed real fixture at cve-db-builder/tests/fixtures/msrc_sample.json. Pure: no network, no database. Full test code, implementation, fixture shape, and three required mutation checks are specified verbatim in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-28-msrc-advisories.md Task 1. Three traps that are easy to get wrong and are each covered by a test: (1) the KB number is Description.Value, NOT SubType — SubType is usually a label like "Security Update" and only sometimes a number, so reading it as the KB yields garbage; (2) products appear BOTH directly on ProductTree.FullProductName and nested inside Branch/Items, and reading only one location silently loses products; (3) CPE vendor and product must be lowercased on parse because MSRC publishes windows_10_21H2 while the NVD dictionary stores windows_10_21h2, and the join fails without it. A product with no CPE must still be recorded. Verified live: 2026-Aug has 1202 vulnerabilities across 282 products, all carrying a CPE.

subject: CIS Benchmark CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 copyleft and commercial distribution barrier (N6)
decision: Reject bundling or distributing CIS Benchmark rules directly in Toonable; pivot N6 configuration compliance to Public Domain DISA STIGs and NIST SP 800-53, while providing a generic open policy engine capable of ingesting operator-supplied rules.
rationale: CIS Benchmarks are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). This imposes two fatal blockers for Toonable: (1) Non-Commercial (NC) clause prohibiting commercial tool distribution without paid CIS SecureSuite Membership, and (2) ShareAlike (SA) copyleft infecting derivative works, violating Toonable's non-negotiable Apache-2.0 / zero-copyleft licensing standard. In contrast, DISA STIGs and NIST guidelines are U.S. Government works placed squarely in the Public Domain (17 U.S.C. § 105).
cost_if_wrong: Using DISA STIGs / NIST SP 800-53 provides open public domain compliance baselines without licensing encumbrance or membership fees, though operators requesting CIS branding by name must supply their own licensed CIS XML/XCCDF files.

Install location prefix matching in package-manager findings marks all CVEs under a product directory as Loaded if a harmless background updater/tray binary is running, causing false reachability promotions.

note: Adversarial review completed. Implementation adheres strictly to FR-83..FR-88 with parameterised queries and report-time risk scoring. Fixing this requires clustering on matched CPE product identities rather than raw registry display strings.

Stale fleet host distortion: stored findings from hosts scanned weeks or months ago are summed into active remediation rankings without temporal decay, giving equal weight to potentially decommissioned or manually patched machines.

Heterogeneous package source confusion: upgrade commands are generated generically per software name, failing for mixed fleets where some assets used winget, some chocolatey, and some raw PE installers.
